subject: Logic
title: The Allais Paradox
description: A quick win: understand The Allais Paradox.

hook.text: People prefer a sure $1 million over a 10% chance of $5 million—but flip their logic in a nearly identical choice.

buildup.text: Maurice Allais showed people violate expected utility theory when certainty is involved.

discovery.text: We overweight certainty. A jump from 99% to 100% feels enormous; 50% to 51% barely registers.

twist.text: This means we don't process probabilities linearly—we warp them based on proximity to certainty.

climax.text: Prospect theory later formalized this: people use a distorted probability scale, not the real one.

punchline.text: Certainty warps probability like gravity warps light.

quiz.question: What does the Allais paradox demonstrate?
options: People overweight certainty and distort probabilities
